title: Simulation of a Voltage-Controlled Voltage Source (VCVS) Circuit Using PySpice

questions.q: What is a Voltage-Controlled Voltage Source (VCVS)?
questions.a: A VCVS is a dependent voltage source whose output terminal voltage is proportional to the voltage difference across a specified pair of controlling nodes.

questions.q: Why doesn't Experiment 3 need a 0 V `Vtest` source like Experiment 2?
questions.a: Because a VCVS senses voltage directly between two existing nodes (Node 2 and Node 3), whereas a CCCS must sense current flowing through a branch.

questions.q: What is the argument order for `circuit.E(1, 4, 5, 2, 3, 3)` in PySpice?
questions.a: Element ID `1`, positive output node `4`, negative output node `5`, positive controlling node `2`, negative controlling node `3`, and voltage gain `3`.

questions.q: Across which resistor is the controlling voltage measured in Experiment 3?
questions.a: Across resistor R3, which is connected between Node 2 and Node 3.

questions.q: Which branches appear in `analysis.branches` for Experiment 3?
questions.a: The independent voltage source `v1` and the dependent voltage source `e1`, since SPICE computes branch currents directly for voltage-defined elements.

questions.q: Why is `V1` connected as `circuit.V(1, 2, 1, 65@u_V)` in Experiment 3?
questions.a: In the manual schematic, V1 is a floating 65 V source with its positive terminal at Node 2 and negative terminal at Node 1.

questions.q: How many non-ground nodes exist in the Experiment 3 VCVS circuit?
What error occurs if the controlling nodes of E1 are swapped from (2, 3) to (3, 2)?
questions.a: The polarity of the dependent voltage source inverts, flipping the sign of V(4) - V(5).

questions.q: Why is Node 1 voltage negative (-25.14 V) in Experiment 3?
questions.a: Because V1 (65 V) has its negative terminal at Node 1 and returns current through R2 (6 Ω) to ground.
